title: Pasting closed and open scalar comparisons with their counits
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, $m,n\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ any unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $T$ use constant module sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $S_T^{A,B}K=K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ for uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$; all scheme maps are $k$-maps [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional functors and their adjunctions on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and ordinary derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Let $W\xrightarrow{t}V\xrightarrow{j}X$ have $t$ closed and $j$ open, and put $h=jt$. Use $Rh_{!,R}=j_{!,R}t_{*,R}$ and $Rh_R^!=Rt_R^!j_R^*$ with counit $\epsilon_{h,R}=\epsilon_{j,R}j_{!,R}(\epsilon_{t,R})$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Suppose given natural closed comparisons $b_t^{A,B}:S_WRt_A^!\to Rt_B^!S_V$ and ordinary closed comparisons $c_t^{A,B}:S_Vt_{*,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}t_{*,B}S_W$ obeying
$$\epsilon_{t,B,S_VK}\,t_{*,B}(b_{t,K}^{A,B})\,c_{t,Rt_A^!K}^{A,B}=S_V(\epsilon_{t,A,K}).$$
Suppose these families obey the identity, successive-scalar and composition-of-closed-immersions cocycles, using the canonical tensor associators and chained exceptional adjunctions. Let $r_j^{A,B}:S_Vj_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j_B^*S_X$ be the canonical restriction comparison, natural and compatible with scalar associativity and identities, and $e_j^{A,B}:S_Xj_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}S_V$ the natural $B$-linear open comparison satisfying $\epsilon_{j,B}j_{!,B}(r_j)e_{j,j_A^*(-)}=S_X(\epsilon_{j,A})$. Assume all indicated operations are defined on the chosen full domains. Define
$$b_{h,M}^{A,B}=Rt_B^!(r_{j,M}^{A,B})\,b_{t,j_A^*M}^{A,B},\qquad c_{h,Q}^{A,B}=j_{!,B}(c_{t,Q}^{A,B})\,e_{j,t_{*,A}Q}^{A,B}.$$
These specified maps are natural, $c_h$ is an isomorphism, and with $N=Rh_A^!M$ they satisfy
$$\epsilon_{h,B,S_XM}\,Rh_{!,B}(b_{h,M}^{A,B})\,c_{h,N}^{A,B}=S_X(\epsilon_{h,A,M}).$$
For any finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, integer $s\ge1$, third finite stage $C=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^s$, and unital map $B\to C$, assuming the corresponding closed and open cocycles, the locally closed maps obey $b_h^{A,C}=b_h^{B,C}S_W^{B,C}(b_h^{A,B})$, with the first factor evaluated at $M_B$. For a further closed immersion $u:W'\hookrightarrow W$, one has
$$b_{jtu,M}^{A,B}=Ru_B^!(b_{jt,M}^{A,B})\,b_{u,R(jt)_A^!M}^{A,B}.$$
The composite counit for this last identity is $\epsilon_j\circ j_!\epsilon_t\circ j_!t_*\epsilon_u$. No invertibility of the closed or locally closed $b$ is a hypothesis or conclusion of this pasting assertion.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, locally closed counit substitution and the two coherence identities; returned steps 11–12

proof.text:
Write $I_R=t_{*,R}$, $T_R=Rt_R^!$, $J_R=j_{!,R}$, $P_R=j_R^*$ for $R=A,B$. Composition is right to left. In calculations with one coefficient map suppress $A,B$ on $b_t,c_t,r_j,e_j,S$. The two given composites have types
$$b_{h,M}:S_WT_AP_AM\longrightarrow T_BP_BS_XM,\qquad c_{h,Q}:S_XJ_AI_AQ\longrightarrow J_BI_BS_WQ.$$
They are natural: for $f:M\to M'$, naturality of $r_j$ and then of $b_t$ gives
$$T_BP_BS_X(f)\,T_B(r_{j,M})b_{t,P_AM}=T_B(r_{j,M'})b_{t,P_AM'}\,S_WT_AP_A(f).$$
For $g:Q\to Q'$, naturality of $c_t$ and then of $e_j$ gives
$$J_BI_BS_W(g)\,J_B(c_{t,Q})e_{j,I_AQ}=J_B(c_{t,Q'})e_{j,I_AQ'}\,S_XJ_AI_A(g).$$
The inverse of $c_{h,Q}$ is $e_{j,I_AQ}^{-1}J_B(c_{t,Q}^{-1})$, because a functor preserves the two inverse equations. This proves the stated naturality and isomorphism assertion without making any assertion about invertibility of $b_h$. All objects and arrows are on the chosen full domains assumed in the statement.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, exceptional counit, closed-composition and successive-scalar coherence (explicit calculation by NO)

proof.text:
Set $K=P_AM$, $N=T_AK$, $D=S_XM$, and let $L$ denote the left side of the desired locally closed counit equation. The composite counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] (Stacks Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits) and the definitions of $b_h,c_h$ give
$$L=\epsilon_{j,B,D}\,J_B\!\left(\epsilon_{t,B,P_BD}\,I_BT_B(r_{j,M})\,I_B(b_{t,K})\,c_{t,N}\right)e_{j,I_AN}.$$
Here $r_{j,M}:S_VK\to P_BD$. Naturality of the counit $\epsilon_{t,B}:I_BT_B\to\mathrm{id}$ at precisely this arrow says
$$\epsilon_{t,B,P_BD}I_BT_B(r_{j,M})=r_{j,M}\epsilon_{t,B,S_VK}.$$
Substitute this equality and then the assumed closed counit equation at $K$ to obtain
$$L=\epsilon_{j,B,D}J_B(r_{j,M})J_B(S_V(\epsilon_{t,A,K}))e_{j,I_AN}.$$
This is substitution of the given normalization equation, not an assertion that the closed comparison is invertible.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, exceptional counit, closed-composition and successive-scalar coherence (explicit calculation by NO)

proof.text:
Naturality of $e_j:S_XJ_A\to J_BS_V$ at $\epsilon_{t,A,K}:I_AN\to K$ gives
$$J_B(S_V(\epsilon_{t,A,K}))e_{j,I_AN}=e_{j,K}\,S_X(J_A(\epsilon_{t,A,K})).$$
Using this equality in the preceding expression for $L$, the assumed open counit equation at $M$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
L&=\epsilon_{j,B,D}J_B(r_{j,M})e_{j,K}\,S_X(J_A(\epsilon_{t,A,K}))\\
 &=S_X(\epsilon_{j,A,M})S_X(J_A(\epsilon_{t,A,K}))\\
 &=S_X\!\left(\epsilon_{j,A,M}J_A(\epsilon_{t,A,P_AM})\right)
 =S_X(\epsilon_{h,A,M}).
\end{aligned}$$
The last identification is exactly the composite counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with $I_A\dashv T_A$ followed by $J_A\dashv P_A$. Thus the equation is for the specified composite adjunction and its actual counit.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, exceptional counit, closed-composition and successive-scalar coherence (explicit calculation by NO)

proof.text:
For successive maps $A\to B\to C$, abbreviate $F_T=S_T^{A,B}$ and $G_T=S_T^{B,C}$. Write $G_TF_T$ for $S_T^{A,C}$ after the canonical tensor associators from the hypotheses, and again put $K=P_AM$. The assumed cocycles say
$$r_{j,M}^{A,C}=r_{j,F_XM}^{B,C}G_V(r_{j,M}^{A,B}),\qquad b_{t,K}^{A,C}=b_{t,F_VK}^{B,C}G_W(b_{t,K}^{A,B}).$$
The arrow $r_{j,M}^{A,B}$ goes from $F_VK$ to $P_BF_XM$. Naturality of $b_t^{B,C}:G_WT_B\to T_CG_V$ at this arrow is
$$T_CG_V(r_{j,M}^{A,B})b_{t,F_VK}^{B,C}=b_{t,P_BF_XM}^{B,C}G_WT_B(r_{j,M}^{A,B}).$$
Expanding $b_h^{A,C}$, using these three equations, and collecting functorial compositions yields
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{h,M}^{A,C}
 &=T_C(r_{j,F_XM}^{B,C})T_CG_V(r_{j,M}^{A,B})b_{t,F_VK}^{B,C}G_W(b_{t,K}^{A,B})\\
 &=T_C(r_{j,F_XM}^{B,C})b_{t,P_BF_XM}^{B,C}G_W\!\left(T_B(r_{j,M}^{A,B})b_{t,K}^{A,B}\right)\\
 &=b_{h,F_XM}^{B,C}G_W(b_{h,M}^{A,B}).
\end{aligned}$$
All associators used here are the same ones with which the two input cocycles were assumed; no new comparison of derived scalar extensions is invoked.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, exceptional counit, closed-composition and successive-scalar coherence (explicit calculation by NO)

proof.text:
For a further closed immersion $u:W'\hookrightarrow W$, write $U_R=Ru_R^!$ and identify $R(tu)_R^!=U_RT_R$ using the chained adjunctions specified in the hypotheses. Closed-composition coherence at $P_AM$ gives
$$b_{tu,P_AM}^{A,B}=U_B(b_{t,P_AM}^{A,B})\,b_{u,T_AP_AM}^{A,B}.$$
The definition for the locally closed factorization $j(tu)$ therefore gives
$$\begin{aligned}
b_{jtu,M}^{A,B}
 &=U_BT_B(r_{j,M}^{A,B})\,U_B(b_{t,P_AM}^{A,B})\,b_{u,T_AP_AM}^{A,B}\\
 &=U_B\!\left(T_B(r_{j,M}^{A,B})b_{t,P_AM}^{A,B}\right)b_{u,T_AP_AM}^{A,B}\\
 &=Ru_B^!(b_{jt,M}^{A,B})\,b_{u,R(jt)_A^!M}^{A,B}.
\end{aligned}$$
For identity coefficient change, the given identity normalizations of $r_j,b_t$ similarly give $b_h^{A,A}=T_A(\mathrm{id})\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$. These are direct functorial substitutions into the specified maps.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: locally closed factorization, exceptional counit, closed-composition and successive-scalar coherence (explicit calculation by NO)

proof.text:
Applying [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] twice to $u_*\dashv Ru^!$, $t_*\dashv Rt^!$, $j_!\dashv j^*$ gives, at coefficient stage $R$ and input $M$,
$$\epsilon_{jtu,R,M}=\epsilon_{j,R,M}\,j_{!,R}(\epsilon_{t,R,j_R^*M})\,j_{!,R}t_{*,R}(\epsilon_{u,R,Rt_R^!j_R^*M}).$$
Indeed composing the first two adjunctions gives the inner counit $\epsilon_t\,t_*\epsilon_u$; applying $j_!$ and then $\epsilon_j$ gives the displayed expression by preservation of composition. Composing the last two first gives the same three factors with the other parentheses. Thus the closed-composition identity in step 5 uses exactly the triple counit asserted in the statement. The calculation in steps 2–3 also applies with the given closed comparison for $tu$, so the locally closed counit equation and this triple-counit description agree. No step cancels, inverts, or assumes invertibility of an exceptional $b$.

lean.note: All clauses are packaged as one theorem for supplied comparisons on actual chosen full domains; definitions have real data and the only postponed proof is this theorem.
